meta.cite: Barton O. Oliver's mTOR Atlas. doi:10.5281/zenodo.22059963

data.mechanism: Sustained cap-dependent translation is what physically builds muscle. Blocking mTOR in humans blunts the protein-synthesis response to exercise.
data.mechanism_beginner: Ongoing protein-building is what physically builds muscle – and in people, blocking mTOR blunts the rise in muscle protein-building after a single bout of exercise. That is the measurement that exists; how much muscle is gained over months under the drug was not measured.
data.context: Requires mechanical load. mTORC1 activation without loading does not reproduce healthy hypertrophy, and constitutive activation alone is not sufficient.
data.boundary: DRU2009 is direct human evidence: rapamycin blocked the contraction-induced rise in muscle protein synthesis in volunteers.
data.note: Rare non-molecular badge in the output branch - DRU2009 is H, a human study.
